title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old Bengaluru security guard, Ratikanta Giri, from Odisha, got a WhatsApp video call on Sept 9. The caller used an AI deepfake to look and sound like Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay and offered Rs 11 lakh in financial aid. A supposed manager said Rs 5 lakh was allotted and asked for fees. Giri first paid Rs 5,000 as exchange charges, then Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN. This is first such case reported in city.

Later, someone claiming to be CBI officer Thakur demanded over Rs 50,000 as a fine. Fearing loss of earlier payments, Giri paid more, totaling over Rs 1.04 lakh through a digital payment app. When fraudsters asked for another Rs 50,000, he refused and realized he was duped. He called cybercrime helpline 1930 and approached Byappanahalli police. A case was registered under the Information Technology Act. Police urged people not to believe such calls or make payments based on such claims.
